ca.title: Aishwarya Rai’s latest Paris appearance looks familiar until you notice this
ca.description: Highlights: Aishwarya Rai unveiled a striking new beauty look in Paris. Her rich burgundy-red hair became one of the evening’s biggest talking points. She paired the dramatic hair transformation with a black velvet couture gown covered in crystal embellishments. L’Oréal’s Audacious Red lipstick complemented her hair and completed the beauty look. Aishwarya shared the L’Oréal Paris runway with several global stars. Aishwarya Rai Bachchan has spent more than two decades commanding international red carpets and fashion runways. But at L'Oréal Paris Le Défilé in Paris on September 28, it was not just her couture gown or diamond headpiece that caught attention. Her burgundy-red hair became the defining detail of the look. Walking at Place Joffre against the backdrop of the Eiffel Tower, the actor appeared in a dramatic black velvet couture creation by Yara Shoemaker, complete with crystals, pearls and a sweeping embellished cape. But the rich, fiery red-burgundy shade of her hair created the strongest contrast against the otherwise dark ensemble. The shade sits between deep burgundy, wine red and fiery red, giving the hair a multidimensional appearance rather than looking like a flat, single-tone colour. Styled with a side parting and soft waves, it framed Aishwarya's face while allowing the colour to remain the central beauty statement. Why Aishwarya's burgundy shade stands out Burgundy is essentially a deep red with brown, purple or wine-toned undertones. It can appear relatively subtle indoors but become much more vibrant under strong lighting, which makes it particularly effective on a fashion runway. In Aishwarya's case, the colour was paired with an almost entirely black outfit. That contrast made the red tones appear even more intense. Instead of competing with the couture, the hair added warmth and colour to the look. And while the exact price of Aishwarya's personal hair-colouring treatment has not been publicly disclosed, burgundy is not necessarily an expensive colour to recreate at home. Current Indian retail listings show burgundy shades ranging from around ₹150 to ₹650 for several mainstream and semi-permanent products. A professional salon treatment, however, can cost considerably more depending on hair length, the technique used, whether pre-lightening is required and the salon's location. There is no verified figure available for what Aishwarya's own colour treatment cost. Aishwarya Rai Bachchan walks the runway during the Le Défilé L'Oréal Paris "Express Your Worth show as part of Paris Fashion Week on September 28, 2026 in Paris, France. Getty Images The red lip completed the transformation The hair was not styled in isolation. Aishwarya paired the burgundy tones with L'Oréal Paris' 423 Audacious Red, the hero shade from the brand's new Runway Matte Collection. The collection features five shades created with Indian skin tones in mind, with Audacious Red positioned as the key shade for the Paris show. The result was a carefully coordinated beauty look: burgundy-red hair, saturated red lips and dramatic black couture. The styling also featured a diamond-encrusted crown-like headpiece, diamond jewellery and matching footwear, adding to the regal character of the appearance. See on Instagram A completely different Aishwarya The burgundy hair also marked a noticeable departure from some of Aishwarya's more familiar beauty looks. Rather than relying on her signature dark hair, the new colour gave her appearance a more dramatic, contemporary edge. The contrast was particularly striking because the rest of the styling remained rooted in classic glamour. The black velvet gown, crystal embellishments and diamond accessories provided the old-world luxury, while the red hair brought the unexpected fashion twist. The approach also fitted the message of L'Oréal Paris' 2026 Le Défilé, themed “Express Your Worth,” which focused on individuality, confidence, diversity and self-expression. Aishwarya has been a L'Oréal Paris ambassador since 2003, and her latest Paris appearance once again placed her at the intersection of fashion and beauty. She shared the runway with stars including Viola Davis, Kendall Jenner, Eva Longoria, Simone Ashley, Jane Fonda and others. But this time, the biggest takeaway from her Paris appearance may be much simpler: a new shade of red can completely change a familiar look.

fr.title: Sûreté de l’IA : Nvidia lance une plateforme pour stopper les agents déviants
fr.description: Nvidia a lancé lundi une plateforme de sécurité dédiée à l’IA qui, selon le géant de l’IA, est capable de contenir des agents indésirables en quelques « millisecondes ». La plateforme Open Agent Safety Platform de ce fabricant de puces et fournisseurs de modèles d’IA doit permettre aux développeurs de définir leurs propres mesures de sécurité pour les agents et de les empêcher de sortir des environnements autorisés. Cette initiative fait suite à une série d’incidents impliquant des agents IA de grands fournisseurs technologiques, notamment OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta et Google, qui ont contourné les contrôles de sécurité pour pirater des systèmes externes lors d'évaluation. Cette situation a suscité un nouvel examen minutieux des garde-fous des systèmes d’IA. Le PDG d’Anthropic, Dario Amodei, a par ailleurs appelé au début du mois les développeurs à changer le rythme des avancées afin de garder les modèles sous contrôle. Ralentir n'est pas le bon terme : Claude Opus 5.5 a été lancé une semaine après cette déclaration. Nvidia considère que ces incidents présentent un schéma commun. Les agents ont contourné les mesures de sécurité intégrées à la couche applicative pour mener à bien les tâches qui leur étaient assignées. Sa plateforme est conçue pour lutter contre ce problème, en fournissant une barrière de sécurité supplémentaire au niveau de l’infrastructure. Ce lancement ne contredit pas le positionnement de Jensen Huang, cofondateur et CEO de Nvidia, estime Kashyap Kompella, CEO et fondateur de RPA2AI Research. Selon l’analyste, les propos du dirigeant de Nvidia ont été surinterprétés en un rejet pur et simple des dangers de l’IA. « Jensen Huang s’est opposé à l’idée selon laquelle rendre l’IA plus sûre nécessite de ralentir son développement », note-t-il. « L’approche de Nvidia consiste justement à faire progresser l’IA tout en mettant en place des contrôles plus stricts autour d’elle ». L'analyste considère que Nvidia a tout à gagner de cette approche. Open Agent Safety Platform constitue à la fois une réponse au problème technique que représentent les risques liés à la sécurité de l’IA et une opportunité commerciale supplémentaire pour Nvidia. Mais Nvidia doit veiller à ce que sa plateforme s’intègre aux systèmes existants de cybersécurité et de gestion des identités, plutôt que de les remplacer, souligne-t-il. Petar Radanliev, spécialiste de la sécurité de l’IA au département d’informatique de l’université d’Oxford, au Royaume-Uni, affirme que le risque va au-delà du simple fait que des agents contournent délibérément les contrôles de sécurité. « Je pense que les agents vont se rebeller. Non pas parce que quelqu’un les a conçus pour cela, mais parce qu’ils peuvent confondre certaines choses », avance-t-il. « L’exécution est excellente, mais le jugement médiocre, et à mon avis, l’exécution s’améliore plus rapidement que le jugement ». Il qualifie la plateforme de Nvidia de « réponse sensée » au problème d’exécution. « Si l’on ne peut pas se fier au jugement d’un agent, on limite ce à quoi il a accès et on le surveille depuis du matériel auquel il ne peut pas toucher », poursuit-il. Nvidia ouvre le capot (et le referme aussitôt) Open Agent Safety Platform se compose de deux éléments principaux. Il y a d'abord OpenShell, une solution open source qui définit les limites d’accès d’un agent. Puis il y a Sentry, une architecture de référence qui s’exécute sur les unités de traitement de données BlueField-4 de Nvidia et offre une couche de contrôle distincte, en dehors de l’environnement logiciel habituel de l’agent. Selon Nvidia, Sentry est capable d’identifier et de mettre en quarantaine un agent qui tente de dépasser les limites qui lui sont autorisées "en moins d’une seconde ». Cette approche vise à répondre à un problème croissant. Les entreprises passent des assistants IA à des agents capables d’intervenir sur l’ensemble des systèmes d’entreprise. Dans un billet publié sur X, le PDG de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, a déclaré que le plein potentiel de l’IA ne pourra être exploité que si les utilisateurs ont la certitude qu’elle est conçue pour être sûre et déployée de manière responsable. Selon Nvidia, plus de 100 fournisseurs et éditeurs collaborent avec elle sur cette plateforme, notamment Anthropic, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, Scale AI, ServiceNow, Palantir et Palo Alto Networks, ainsi que des entreprises de robotique telles que Figure, Gecko Robotics et Skild AI. OpenShell, qui fonctionne avec des systèmes d’IA ouverts et propriétaires, est désormais disponible via les ressources pour développeurs de Nvidia et sur GitHub. C’est un runtime privé pour orchestrer une flotte d’agents IA. Chaque agent est exécuté dans un sandbox, un environnement isolé, les règles sont appliquées à l’échelle du kernel, sur les puces Vera. Quant à la plateforme Open Agent Safety, elle permet d’étendre les mesures de sécurité au-delà de l’environnement agentique : OpenShell restreint l’accès aux identifiants, aux réseaux, aux fichiers et aux outils, tandis que Sentry assure une surveillance et une application supplémentaires. De plus, le fait qu’OpenShell soit ouvert et indépendant de tout modèle attirera les développeurs et les entreprises à la recherche d’un système de surveillance plus rigoureux. Cependant, l’un des défis réside dans le fait que, même si un agent est soumis à des restrictions et confiné, il peut tout de même se comporter de manière inappropriée. « Un agent peut respecter toutes les limites techniques et pourtant prendre une mauvaise décision, mal interpréter une tâche ou abuser des autorisations qui lui ont été légitimement accordées », affirme Kashyap Kompella. L'efficacité de l'approche de Nvidia reste incertaine Petar Radanliev prévient que l'efficacité de la plateforme n'avait pas encore été démontrée. « Personne, pas même Nvidia, ne peut encore prouver qu'une de ces plateformes fonctionne », lance-t-il. « Il n'existe ni référence commune ni tests comparatifs publiés. Les acheteurs comparent les architectures, pas les résultats ». De fait, OpenShell est en version 0.1.2, tandis que le design de référence de Sentry n’est pas publiquement disponible. Le nom n’a d’ailleurs rien à voir avec la suite de monitoring éponyme. « La surveillance en temps réel permet de détecter un agent qui enfreint une règle. Elle est en revanche bien moins efficace pour repérer un agent qui se trompe en toute confiance », nuance Petar Radanliev. Pour les entreprises qui déploient des agents, cela signifie que les contrôles de sécurité doivent aller au-delà de la simple surveillance des actions des agents. « Ne partez pas du principe qu’un agent compétent est forcément un agent sensé », avance-t-il. « Laissez à l’humain le soin de prendre les décisions irréversibles, car c’est précisément là que les agents sont les plus faibles ». Il recommande également de vérifier ce que les agents mémorisent et communiquent entre eux, ainsi que de s’assurer que les organisations puissent remonter à la source des erreurs. « Si vous ne pouvez pas remonter à la source d’une erreur, vous ne pouvez pas trouver l’agent dormant », poursuit-il.

es.title: España, a por el liderato en solitario con rotaciones
es.description: España tiene otro hueso duro de roer en su camino hacia el play-off de la UEFA Nations League , previo paso a la Final Four que da opciones a luchar por el título. Después de ganar a Inglaterra, el equipo español se enfrenta a una Croacia que inicia un nuevo ciclo en el banquillo con Slaven Bilic después de los años dorados de Zlatko Dalic. El conjunto español no pudo estrenar de mejor forma su segunda estrella ofreciendo un magnífico espectáclo en Wembley con un Lamine Yamal deslumbrante (2-3) . Ahora toca otro reto mayúsculo ante un rival siempre competitivo. De la Fuente situó en Londres a su once de gala, pero ahora debe optar por las rotaciones. El desgaste fue muy grande y es obligado el cambio de jugadores. Ninguna posición está libre de poder sufrir un relevo, dada la intención del míster riojano de repartir las cargas de minutos. Todas las líneas Pese a ello, en la portería todo apunta que seguirá Unai Simón por delante de David Raya y Josep Martínez . El dilema llega en defensa. Con la lesión de Eric Garcia , Marc Pubill tuvo que jugar de lateral derecho y ahora se ha incorporado Robin Le Normand a la convocatoria. Una opción muy probable es que el joven Iván Fresneda, del Sporting Club de Portugal, tenga su oportunidad. Image ID: 134756415 Fresneda puede aportar velocidad por la banda derecha de España ante Croacia Dennis Agyeman / AFP7 / Europa P / Europa Press /clip/ecc6fddb-ba4e-4173-81a2-0968e84ba108_source-aspect-ratio_default_0_x1000y444.jpg 2000 1333 En el eje podría entrar el madridista Huijsen , mientras que en el lateral izquierdo por fin puede llegar la oportunidad para Grimaldo . El jugador del Atlético de Madrid se quedó sin participar en el Mundial y tampoco lo hizo en Wembley, por lo que De la Fuente lo quiere recompensar. Cucurella tendría así descanso. Más difícil parece que Cubarsí se quede en el banquillo, dadas sus altas prestaciones. Pedri y Fermín En el centro del campo, Rodri podría dejar su puesto a Zubimendi, con Pedri actuando de interior y quizá Fermín de media punta . El onubense calentó en Londres, pero no tuvo minutos. La ventaja de Fermín es que puede actuar tanto de media punta o como en la banda izquierda , si bien esta posición parece destinada a Álex Baena después de su gran encuentro ante Inglaterra cuando entró en la segunda parte. Image ID: 134756460 Los jugdores españoles están preparados para rotar Rodrigo Jimenez / EFE /clip/3f6f4c45-6d41-404c-af08-fb883c523d5d_source-aspect-ratio_default_0_x1000y444.jpg 2000 1333 En ataque no hay dudas sobre la presencia de Lamine Yamal . El que puede ser próximo Balón de Oro tendría la compañía de Oyarzabal, con 30 goles ya con la selección, y del propio Baena . Sería la misma delantera que salió de inicio en la final del Mundial en Nueva Jersey. A por el partido 41 sin perder En cualquier caso, la ventaja de De la Fuente es de contar con una plantilla que siempre le ha rendido con independencia de los cambios que haya efectuado. El técnico puede permitirse el lujo de rotar como se ha visto con el rendimiento del equipo en los 40 partidos que lleva sin perder en competición oficial. Los duelos entre España y Croacia ya se han convertido en unos clásicos del fútbol moderno. La Roja ha salido airosa la mayoría de ocasiones, con un único tropiezo significativo en la Eurocopa del 2016, con un gol de Perisic, que envió al equipo que dirigía aún Vicente del Bosque al lado difícil de los cruces, cayendo ante Italia en París. España ha realizado partidos memorables frente a los croatas como un 6-0 en Elche en 2018 también en la UEFA Nations League o un vibrante 5-3 en la Eurocopa del 2021 con Luis Enrique en el banquillo. El partido ha levantado una gran expectación y se espera un lleno en el Sánchez Pizjuán para ver a los bicampeones del mundo . España hace disfrutar a la afición y su presencia levanta pasiones. La conquista del último Mundial ha sido la guinda para un gran equipo que se ha ganado el corazón de la 'marea roja'. mx.title: BRSK1: 10 casos muestran síntomas más allá de la epilepsia
mx.description: ✨︎ Resumen (TL;DR): Baylor College of Medicine y otras instituciones analizaron 10 personas con variantes de BRSK1, reunidas en siete familias no emparentadas . Todas presentaban retraso del desarrollo, pero solo dos participantes habían tenido convulsiones. AI-MARRVEL y experimentos en moscas de la fruta aportaron evidencia de que algunas variantes reducen la función de BRSK1, aunque no definen un tratamiento. Investigadores de Baylor College of Medicine y otras instituciones ampliaron los síntomas asociados a BRSK1 al estudiar a 10 personas con retraso del desarrollo; solo dos habían tenido convulsiones. El trabajo se publicó en The American Journal of Human Genetics y combinó una herramienta de inteligencia artificial para priorizar variantes genéticas con experimentos en moscas de la fruta, que aportaron evidencia de que algunas variantes reducen la función del gen. El estudio no establece un tratamiento. Te podría interesar: Edición genética frena epilepsia severa en ratones Foto: Joel De Leon / Pexels Los síntomas no se limitaron a las convulsiones Las 10 personas estudiadas presentaban algún grado de retraso del desarrollo. Entre las características observadas estuvieron: Dificultades del lenguaje . Discapacidad intelectual . Rasgos de autismo . Trastorno por déficit de atención e hiperactividad . Bajo tono muscular . Microcefalia . La intensidad de los síntomas variaba incluso entre familiares con la misma variante. Por ahora, esta variabilidad no permite anticipar cómo se manifestará cada variante en una persona. Solo dos participantes habían tenido convulsiones. Ese dato no establece la frecuencia de la epilepsia entre todas las personas con variantes de BRSK1. El vínculo de BRSK1 con la epilepsia ya estaba descrito Un estudio publicado en Epilepsia en octubre de 2025 relacionó BRSK1 con epilepsia y trastornos del neurodesarrollo. La investigación partió de 394 familias con epilepsia sin causa identificada, describió ocho personas afectadas con variantes del gen y encontró mayor susceptibilidad a convulsiones en ratones con actividad reducida de Brsk1 . Ambos trabajos reunieron grupos pequeños mediante criterios distintos. El estudio de Epilepsia buscó familias con epilepsia; la nueva serie partió de casos sin diagnóstico y de una red internacional de investigadores. Por eso, los datos no permiten convertir las dos personas con convulsiones de esta serie en una tasa de epilepsia para todas las personas con variantes de BRSK1. Cómo la IA encontró la variante candidata El caso inicial correspondió a un menor inscrito en el Texome Project. El análisis genético convencional del menor y uno de sus progenitores no ofreció una respuesta. AI-MARRVEL es una herramienta de inteligencia artificial que prioriza variantes genéticas candidatas. En este caso, destacó una variante poco frecuente de BRSK1 . El equipo compartió el hallazgo en GeneMatcher, localizó otras familias con variantes del mismo gen y reunió los 10 casos, según Baylor College of Medicine. Las moscas pusieron a prueba la función de BRSK1 Para examinar la posible relación biológica, los investigadores estudiaron sff , el equivalente de BRSK1 en moscas de la fruta. Al desactivar sff, las moscas desarrollaron problemas de movimiento y mayor sensibilidad a condiciones que desencadenaban comportamientos parecidos a convulsiones. Introducir una copia humana normal de BRSK1 corrigió gran parte de las alteraciones. Las variantes encontradas en los pacientes solo lograron una recuperación parcial. Ese contraste aportó evidencia de que algunas variantes reducen la función del gen. Los experimentos también mostraron cambios en las conexiones entre nervios y músculos y un aumento de una proteína vinculada con los microtúbulos, estructuras internas de las células. Los autores proponen que esa alteración podría contribuir a los problemas del neurodesarrollo. La evidencia proviene de moscas y no demuestra directamente ese mecanismo en el cerebro de los participantes. Qué permite concluir la evidencia La combinación de casos humanos y pruebas funcionales refuerza la utilidad de considerar BRSK1 al investigar cuadros del neurodesarrollo sin diagnóstico. La serie reúne solo 10 personas , y los síntomas varían incluso entre familiares con la misma variante. Por ahora, el estudio no permite predecir cómo se manifestará cada variante ni extraer de estos experimentos una terapia. mx.title: La app de Smart TV con mejores canales gratis se actualiza a lo grande con una nueva experiencia y novedades
mx.description: La aplicación para Smart TV que usan miles de personas en todo el mundo para ver canales gratis , está de estreno. Y lo hace con una nueva experiencia de usuario que cambia la forma de usar la app, mientras que también se introducen otros cambios y novedades importantes. Mes a mes, incluso con la expansión que está viviendo el mercado de los canales gratis, Pluto TV se ha mantenido como la principal referencia del sector. Lo ha hecho gracias a una sólida estrategia de contenidos, lanzando nuevos canales dedicados a series famosas y todo tipo de películas o incluso deportes. Ahora vuelven a marcar tendencias con el estreno de una nueva experiencia de usuario. ¿Cómo es ahora Pluto TV? Si entras en Pluto TV, ya sea con tu navegador o desde una Smart TV , verás cambios al instante. Lo primero que se aprecia es que la interfaz es más moderna, intuitiva y flexible. A Pluto TV siempre se le había criticado por ser un servicio con una interfaz lenta y compleja, así que este cambio de imagen es algo que le sienta bien. Pluto TV estrena una nueva interfaz. / Captura propia: Web de Pluto TV Además del cambio de diseño, lo más importante de esta nueva experiencia es que ahora ofrece un alto nivel de personalización. Lo que busca Pluto TV es que los usuarios se sientan más a gusto dentro de la aplicación y que tengan más motivos para estar dentro de ella viendo contenidos. Entre otras cosas, se crea una mejor dinámica entre los canales lineales que están disponibles y los contenidos bajo demanda, como películas y series. Los usuarios normalmente combinan ambos tipos de reproducción, así que Pluto TV no quiere dejar de lado ninguna de sus dos propuestas. Novedades destacadas La lentitud con la que cargaba la rejilla de canales de Pluto TV siempre había sido uno de sus mayores problemas. El sistema de favoritos también era algo que resultaba un problema, así que ahora la aplicación permite marcar tus canales preferidos de una manera eficiente. La guía de canales es mucho más rápida, más clara y está mejor ordenada. Lo mismo se puede decir del acceso a la programación de cada canal, permitiendo ver lo que van a echar posteriormente más allá de simplemente las próximas horas. Aunque hay muchos canales donde la programación no cambia mucho, es necesario saber qué episodios emitirán después para tener claro cuándo nos gustaría cambiar de canal. Pluto TV introduce una mejor presentación de sus canales. / Captura propia: Web de Pluto TV Otra mejora significativa de la aplicación se encuentra en la posibilidad de combinar e intercalar la reproducción de contenidos bajo demanda y canales. Así, podemos movernos libremente por la plataforma al completo incluso si tenemos un contenido bajo reproducción. Pluto TV también ha añadido una lista de seguimiento más completa y personalizable , búsqueda unificada y reinicio del programa con un solo clic. El objetivo es aumentar la facilidad de uso y que así haya más personas que disfruten de la experiencia.

in.title: Coway Run 2026 Celebrates a Decade of Progress as Thousands of Malaysians Run Forward Without Limits at Stadium Merdeka
in.description: Marking a decade of momentum, the 10th edition of Coway Run continues to inspire Malaysians to pursue continuous growth and move forward without limits KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coway, the Best Life Solution Company, brought together more than 11,000 participants at Stadium Merdeka for the 10th edition of Coway Run 2026, a milestone event that celebrated a decade of inspiring Malaysians to embrace healthier lifestyles, push beyond their perceived limits and unlock their full potential. Coway Malaysia's management team officially flagging off the 10KM Run Category at Coway Run 2026, marking the start of a race dedicated to moving Forward Without Limits. Fuelled by the excitement of Coway Malaysia's 20th anniversary, this year's event carried the theme Forward Without Limits, reflecting Coway's belief that growth is an ongoing journey and that every individual has the ability to achieve more through determination, perseverance and continuous self-improvement. More than a running event, Coway Run 2026 served as a platform for people from all walks of life to challenge themselves, celebrate personal milestones and take meaningful steps towards becoming the best versions of themselves. Janice Tan, Group Manager of Marketing Division of Coway Malaysia said, "This year's Coway Run holds special significance as we celebrate both 20 years of Coway in Malaysia and 10 years of Coway Run. Over the past decade, we have seen individuals from all backgrounds come together, set new goals and push beyond what they thought was possible. At Coway, we believe that everyone possesses untapped potential, and Coway Run was created to inspire people to take that first step towards unlocking it." "The theme 'Forward Without Limits' reflects our conviction that progress is not defined by perfect conditions, but by the courage and determination to keep moving forward despite the obstacles along the way. Even in the rain, we saw many runners choosing to persevere and complete their journey, embodying the very spirit of resilience that this year's event set out to celebrate. It was inspiring to see thousands of Malaysians come together, not only to challenge themselves but also support a cause that creates a meaningful impact for communities in need," she added. With the health and safety of participants as the highest priority, Coway Run 2026 took an unexpected turn this year as the event adapted to the challenges posed by the weather and ongoing haze situation. Despite the change in format, participants from all four categories, including the 10KM Run, and modified 30KM Run, 5KM Run and 5KM Kids Run, came together with community spirit, embodying the "Forward Without Limits" philosophy. Throughout the day, the atmosphere extended beyond the race routes as participants, families and supporters immersed themselves in a vibrant race village featuring interactive activities, engaging experiences and family-friendly entertainment. The event embodied Coway's commitment to making healthy living both accessible and enjoyable, while creating opportunities for meaningful connections among communities. Inside Stadium Merdeka, visitors enjoyed a special performance by Coway's Biddy Bear mascot and dancers, followed by a live performance and exclusive meet-and-greet with popular Malaysian singer and actor Hael Husaini. Participants could also complete eight game stations to enter a grand prize lucky draw, with 10 winners taking home either a BEREX Massage Bed or BEREX Pebble Chair, while limited-edition Coway Biddy Bear hand towels were available to be won through on-ground games. In keeping with Coway's mission of helping people live healthier and happier lives, Coway Run 2026 continued to create impact beyond race day. RM10 from every ticket sold will be channeled towards the Coway Happy Water Project, an initiative dedicated to providing underserved communities with access to clean water. Through the collective efforts of participants, every registration contributed towards improving quality of life for communities in need and supporting a future where access to essential resources is within reach for all. Beyond making a meaningful difference for communities, Coway Run 2026 celebrated the perseverance and resilience demonstrated by participants in the face of unexpected circumstances. Reflecting the event's "Forward Without Limits" philosophy, runners continued to push forward and delivered inspiring performances across the competitive categories. In the Men's Open Malaysian category of the modified 30KM Run, conducted over a 10KM route, Anas Bin Rosli recorded the fastest finishing time of 00:36:27, while Michelle Ng claimed the Women's Open Malaysian title with a time of 00:54:24. In the 10KM category, Khairul Hazwan secured first place in the Men's Open Malaysian division with a time of 00:40:46, while Ee Pui Yin topped the Women's Open Malaysian category with a finishing time of 00:43:27. As Coway Run enters its second decade, the event continues to reflect Coway's commitment to empowering individuals to lead healthier lives, pursue meaningful growth and realise their potential. For more information and updates on Coway, please visit https://www.coway.com.my/ . About Coway Malaysia Coway, the Best Life Solution Company Established in 1989, Coway has been the indisputable market leader in the manufacturing and distribution of well-being household appliances in South Korea, thanks to its largest indoor water purifier manufacturing plant in the world, and state-of-the-art R&D centre in Seoul National University. Famous for its home products, Coway has been aggressively expanding its business worldwide and has over 11 million customers across the world. Besides earning recognition for its high-quality range of products, Coway is also known for its excellent after-sales customer service, and innovative easy payment plan. In 2006, Coway was introduced into the Malaysian market. Having been in Malaysia for 20 years, Coway has reached millions of Malaysian customers and has been successfully recognised as the Best Life Solution Company that strives to provide cleaner water, fresher air and better sleep; encouraging people to "Change Your Life" towards leading healthier and happier lives.

sg.title: Sino Group and SVhk Connect Start-ups with Northern Metropolis Communities Through 'Impactathon'
sg.description: To Co-create Technology Solutions for Community Well-being HONG KONG , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Northern Metropolis is steadily emerging as one of Hong Kong's key growth areas. As development gathers pace, communities have diverse and evolving needs in areas such as older adults' well-being, youth development, community connection, and social inclusion. To gain a deeper understanding of these needs and explore practical responses, Sino Inno Lab and The Spark under Sino Group have partnered with Social Ventures Hong Kong (SVhk) to launch the 'SVhk-Sino Impactathon'. The initiative brings together start-ups, universities, community organisations and residents to explore how innovation and technology can support everyday life, generating practical insights through community engagement and pilot projects to inform the Northern Metropolis's long-term development. The initiative is supported by the Northern Metropolis Co-ordination Office (NMCO) of the Development Bureau of the HKSAR Government, over 10 start-ups, six local universities, and various community partners, bringing together more than 50 partners in total. It has connected over 1,000 Northern Metropolis residents and stakeholders, including children, youth, underprivileged families, older adults and rehabilitation service users. Direct engagement has provided participating teams with valuable perspectives that have helped refine their solutions for practical application. Turning Ideas into Community Solutions Unlike conventional start-up competitions, the 'SVhk-Sino Impactathon' was designed to help innovators better understand the communities they hope to serve. Over five months, participating teams worked alongside seven community partners and engaged directly with residents to gain first-hand insights into local aspirations and community needs. The programme was supported by organisations including the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation and the Jockey Club Design Institute for Social Innovation at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, together with entrepreneurship and innovation platforms from City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Baptist University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and The University of Hong Kong. These collaborations have enabled start-ups to explore how their technologies could address community needs in real-world settings. Participating teams applied technologies including artificial intelligence ('AI'), geographic information systems ('GIS'), biotechnology and food technology to address challenges ranging from older adults' health and fall-risk prevention to youth learning and family well-being. Feedback from residents and frontline organisations has helped teams refine their solutions and improve their practical relevance. The programme also attracted start-ups from seven Asian cities, with three regional teams advancing to the finals and travelling to Hong Kong to exchange ideas with local communities and partners, while also gaining insights into the Northern Metropolis. Supporting the Development of Promising Solutions The award ceremony was held at One North in Yuen Long, where 11 teams presented their pilot projects and shared plans for future development. To support the further refinement and real-world application of selected solutions, a total of HK$200,000 in seed funding was awarded to winning teams. GOFA received the Grand Prize and Most Innovative Award for its AI-powered health risk assessment technology, while Mapcraft received the Most Community-Driven Award, and Singapore-based start-up N&E Innovations received the Most Scalable Builder Award. At the award ceremony, residents from different backgrounds, including ethnic minority communities, older adults, children, young people and families from the Northern Metropolis, were invited to experience the projects developed by participating start-ups and universities. Interactive workshops, demonstrations and sharing sessions allowed residents to explore innovative solutions first-hand and provide direct feedback to the innovators, helping inform their future development and application. Mr Ronald Cheng, Principal Assistant Secretary (Northern Metropolis) of the NMCO, who was invited to attend the award ceremony, stated, 'Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proposes that we will guide the future spatial layout of our city with the vision of the "South North Dual Engine (Finance IT)". The Northern Metropolis will be developed with the objectives of university town, I&T, industry, and environment suitable for living, work, and travel. This will require innovative thinking and cross-sector collaboration. The "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" has enabled start-up teams to step into the community, thereby understanding residents' actual needs and proposing targeted solutions. We are pleased to see that the business sector, academia, community organisations and start-ups have been working hand-in-hand on new ideas to contribute to the development of the Northern Metropolis.' Mr Francis Ngai, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of SVhk, shared, 'Community making requires both hardware and software infrastructure. While the physical infrastructure of the Northern Metropolis is gradually taking shape, its community infrastructure should be built with equal urgency to support thriving neighbourhoods. The needs of older adults, children and youth, agricultural transformation, circular economy and social inclusion also point to new reimaginations for the communities of tomorrow, and call for parallel learning and experimentation as Hong Kong advances its innovation-and-technology and talent-development priorities. The "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" brings together cross-sector partners to identify local needs, work with universities and innovation partners to find suitable solutions, and match them with frontline organisations for real-world testing and refinement. We hope each trial will generate shared learnings within the Northern Metropolis, and build, from the bottom up, the community's capacity to listen, collaborate and address challenges together.' Mr David Ng, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of Sino Group, said, 'As the Northern Metropolis continues to grow and evolve, so too do the needs of its communities. We believe the value of innovation lies not in technology alone, but in how it can improve people's lives. Building on last year's "One North STEAM AI Summer", we launched the "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" to bring together partners across government, industry, academia, research institutions and the community to explore practical solutions that support community well-being. We are grateful to all our partners, community organisations, universities, start-ups and residents for their support, and look forward to seeing these ideas continue to evolve and make a positive impact on communities across the Northern Metropolis.' ph.title: Coway Run 2026 Celebrates a Decade of Progress as Thousands of Malaysians Run Forward Without Limits at Stadium Merdeka
ph.description: Marking a decade of momentum, the 10th edition of Coway Run continues to inspire Malaysians to pursue continuous growth and move forward without limits KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coway, the Best Life Solution Company, brought together more than 11,000 participants at Stadium Merdeka for the 10th edition of Coway Run 2026, a milestone event that celebrated a decade of inspiring Malaysians to embrace healthier lifestyles, push beyond their perceived limits and unlock their full potential. Coway Malaysia's management team officially flagging off the 10KM Run Category at Coway Run 2026, marking the start of a race dedicated to moving Forward Without Limits. Fuelled by the excitement of Coway Malaysia's 20th anniversary, this year's event carried the theme Forward Without Limits, reflecting Coway's belief that growth is an ongoing journey and that every individual has the ability to achieve more through determination, perseverance and continuous self-improvement. More than a running event, Coway Run 2026 served as a platform for people from all walks of life to challenge themselves, celebrate personal milestones and take meaningful steps towards becoming the best versions of themselves. Janice Tan, Group Manager of Marketing Division of Coway Malaysia said, "This year's Coway Run holds special significance as we celebrate both 20 years of Coway in Malaysia and 10 years of Coway Run. Over the past decade, we have seen individuals from all backgrounds come together, set new goals and push beyond what they thought was possible. At Coway, we believe that everyone possesses untapped potential, and Coway Run was created to inspire people to take that first step towards unlocking it." "The theme 'Forward Without Limits' reflects our conviction that progress is not defined by perfect conditions, but by the courage and determination to keep moving forward despite the obstacles along the way. Even in the rain, we saw many runners choosing to persevere and complete their journey, embodying the very spirit of resilience that this year's event set out to celebrate. It was inspiring to see thousands of Malaysians come together, not only to challenge themselves but also support a cause that creates a meaningful impact for communities in need," she added. With the health and safety of participants as the highest priority, Coway Run 2026 took an unexpected turn this year as the event adapted to the challenges posed by the weather and ongoing haze situation. Despite the change in format, participants from all four categories, including the 10KM Run, and modified 30KM Run, 5KM Run and 5KM Kids Run, came together with community spirit, embodying the "Forward Without Limits" philosophy. Throughout the day, the atmosphere extended beyond the race routes as participants, families and supporters immersed themselves in a vibrant race village featuring interactive activities, engaging experiences and family-friendly entertainment. The event embodied Coway's commitment to making healthy living both accessible and enjoyable, while creating opportunities for meaningful connections among communities. Inside Stadium Merdeka, visitors enjoyed a special performance by Coway's Biddy Bear mascot and dancers, followed by a live performance and exclusive meet-and-greet with popular Malaysian singer and actor Hael Husaini. Participants could also complete eight game stations to enter a grand prize lucky draw, with 10 winners taking home either a BEREX Massage Bed or BEREX Pebble Chair, while limited-edition Coway Biddy Bear hand towels were available to be won through on-ground games. In keeping with Coway's mission of helping people live healthier and happier lives, Coway Run 2026 continued to create impact beyond race day. RM10 from every ticket sold will be channeled towards the Coway Happy Water Project, an initiative dedicated to providing underserved communities with access to clean water. Through the collective efforts of participants, every registration contributed towards improving quality of life for communities in need and supporting a future where access to essential resources is within reach for all. Beyond making a meaningful difference for communities, Coway Run 2026 celebrated the perseverance and resilience demonstrated by participants in the face of unexpected circumstances. Reflecting the event's "Forward Without Limits" philosophy, runners continued to push forward and delivered inspiring performances across the competitive categories. In the Men's Open Malaysian category of the modified 30KM Run, conducted over a 10KM route, Anas Bin Rosli recorded the fastest finishing time of 00:36:27, while Michelle Ng claimed the Women's Open Malaysian title with a time of 00:54:24. In the 10KM category, Khairul Hazwan secured first place in the Men's Open Malaysian division with a time of 00:40:46, while Ee Pui Yin topped the Women's Open Malaysian category with a finishing time of 00:43:27. As Coway Run enters its second decade, the event continues to reflect Coway's commitment to empowering individuals to lead healthier lives, pursue meaningful growth and realise their potential. For more information and updates on Coway, please visit https://www.coway.com.my/ . About Coway Malaysia Coway, the Best Life Solution Company Established in 1989, Coway has been the indisputable market leader in the manufacturing and distribution of well-being household appliances in South Korea, thanks to its largest indoor water purifier manufacturing plant in the world, and state-of-the-art R&D centre in Seoul National University. Famous for its home products, Coway has been aggressively expanding its business worldwide and has over 11 million customers across the world. Besides earning recognition for its high-quality range of products, Coway is also known for its excellent after-sales customer service, and innovative easy payment plan. In 2006, Coway was introduced into the Malaysian market. Having been in Malaysia for 20 years, Coway has reached millions of Malaysian customers and has been successfully recognised as the Best Life Solution Company that strives to provide cleaner water, fresher air and better sleep; encouraging people to "Change Your Life" towards leading healthier and happier lives.

ph.title: Sino Group and SVhk Connect Start-ups with Northern Metropolis Communities Through 'Impactathon'
ph.description: To Co-create Technology Solutions for Community Well-being HONG KONG , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Northern Metropolis is steadily emerging as one of Hong Kong's key growth areas. As development gathers pace, communities have diverse and evolving needs in areas such as older adults' well-being, youth development, community connection, and social inclusion. To gain a deeper understanding of these needs and explore practical responses, Sino Inno Lab and The Spark under Sino Group have partnered with Social Ventures Hong Kong (SVhk) to launch the 'SVhk-Sino Impactathon'. The initiative brings together start-ups, universities, community organisations and residents to explore how innovation and technology can support everyday life, generating practical insights through community engagement and pilot projects to inform the Northern Metropolis's long-term development. The initiative is supported by the Northern Metropolis Co-ordination Office (NMCO) of the Development Bureau of the HKSAR Government, over 10 start-ups, six local universities, and various community partners, bringing together more than 50 partners in total. It has connected over 1,000 Northern Metropolis residents and stakeholders, including children, youth, underprivileged families, older adults and rehabilitation service users. Direct engagement has provided participating teams with valuable perspectives that have helped refine their solutions for practical application. Turning Ideas into Community Solutions Unlike conventional start-up competitions, the 'SVhk-Sino Impactathon' was designed to help innovators better understand the communities they hope to serve. Over five months, participating teams worked alongside seven community partners and engaged directly with residents to gain first-hand insights into local aspirations and community needs. The programme was supported by organisations including the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation and the Jockey Club Design Institute for Social Innovation at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, together with entrepreneurship and innovation platforms from City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Baptist University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and The University of Hong Kong. These collaborations have enabled start-ups to explore how their technologies could address community needs in real-world settings. Participating teams applied technologies including artificial intelligence ('AI'), geographic information systems ('GIS'), biotechnology and food technology to address challenges ranging from older adults' health and fall-risk prevention to youth learning and family well-being. Feedback from residents and frontline organisations has helped teams refine their solutions and improve their practical relevance. The programme also attracted start-ups from seven Asian cities, with three regional teams advancing to the finals and travelling to Hong Kong to exchange ideas with local communities and partners, while also gaining insights into the Northern Metropolis. Supporting the Development of Promising Solutions The award ceremony was held at One North in Yuen Long, where 11 teams presented their pilot projects and shared plans for future development. To support the further refinement and real-world application of selected solutions, a total of HK$200,000 in seed funding was awarded to winning teams. GOFA received the Grand Prize and Most Innovative Award for its AI-powered health risk assessment technology, while Mapcraft received the Most Community-Driven Award, and Singapore-based start-up N&E Innovations received the Most Scalable Builder Award. At the award ceremony, residents from different backgrounds, including ethnic minority communities, older adults, children, young people and families from the Northern Metropolis, were invited to experience the projects developed by participating start-ups and universities. Interactive workshops, demonstrations and sharing sessions allowed residents to explore innovative solutions first-hand and provide direct feedback to the innovators, helping inform their future development and application. Mr Ronald Cheng, Principal Assistant Secretary (Northern Metropolis) of the NMCO, who was invited to attend the award ceremony, stated, 'Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proposes that we will guide the future spatial layout of our city with the vision of the "South North Dual Engine (Finance IT)". The Northern Metropolis will be developed with the objectives of university town, I&T, industry, and environment suitable for living, work, and travel. This will require innovative thinking and cross-sector collaboration. The "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" has enabled start-up teams to step into the community, thereby understanding residents' actual needs and proposing targeted solutions. We are pleased to see that the business sector, academia, community organisations and start-ups have been working hand-in-hand on new ideas to contribute to the development of the Northern Metropolis.' Mr Francis Ngai, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of SVhk, shared, 'Community making requires both hardware and software infrastructure. While the physical infrastructure of the Northern Metropolis is gradually taking shape, its community infrastructure should be built with equal urgency to support thriving neighbourhoods. The needs of older adults, children and youth, agricultural transformation, circular economy and social inclusion also point to new reimaginations for the communities of tomorrow, and call for parallel learning and experimentation as Hong Kong advances its innovation-and-technology and talent-development priorities. The "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" brings together cross-sector partners to identify local needs, work with universities and innovation partners to find suitable solutions, and match them with frontline organisations for real-world testing and refinement. We hope each trial will generate shared learnings within the Northern Metropolis, and build, from the bottom up, the community's capacity to listen, collaborate and address challenges together.' Mr David Ng, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of Sino Group, said, 'As the Northern Metropolis continues to grow and evolve, so too do the needs of its communities. We believe the value of innovation lies not in technology alone, but in how it can improve people's lives. Building on last year's "One North STEAM AI Summer", we launched the "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" to bring together partners across government, industry, academia, research institutions and the community to explore practical solutions that support community well-being. We are grateful to all our partners, community organisations, universities, start-ups and residents for their support, and look forward to seeing these ideas continue to evolve and make a positive impact on communities across the Northern Metropolis.' Download images: please click here The award ceremony for the ‘SVhk-Sino Impactathon’ was recently held at One North in Yuen Long. The programme was supported by the Northern Metropolis Co-ordination Office of the Development Bureau of the HKSAR Government, over 10 start-ups, six local universities and various community partners, bringing together more than 50 partners in total. Through interactive workshops, technology experience booths, and demonstrations, the ‘SVhk-Sino Impactathon’ enabled participants to explore innovative technologies in an engaging, interactive setting.

ph.title: Watch: Haze, air quality worsens in Singapore as fires rage in neighbouring Indonesia
ph.description: Haze, air quality worsens in Singapore as fires rage in neighbouring Indonesia Air quality in Singapore worsens on Sept. 29, 2026 as the country wakes up to unhealthy levels of air pollution due to forest fires in neighboring Indonesia. As of 9 a.m. local time (0100 GMT), data from Swiss monitoring website IQAir showed a reading of 179, which falls under the unhealthy range. Indonesia is battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, and its Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni has warned that the wildfires could continue until November this year. The islands of Borneo and Sumatra have been the worst hit, with the hazardous haze causing a spike in respiratory illnesses. Transboundary haze has also created unhealthy air conditions in neighboring Malaysia. ph.title: vivo V80 Lite sets world record with 32-hour livestream
ph.description: The vivo V80 Lite has set a GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS title after completing a 32-hour and 37-minute continuous livestream, marking a new milestone for the upcoming smartphone. The livestream, conducted on August 11, 2026, in Chiang Mai, Thailand, earned the title of “The Longest Electronic Product Live Stream.” The V80 Lite remained operational throughout the challenge without interruption, putting its endurance through more than a full day of continuous broadcasting. The record attempt was independently observed under GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS guidelines, with the 32-hour, 37-minute livestream providing a measurable test of how long the device could sustain an intensive, uninterrupted activity. Southeast Asian creators put the phone to the test The record-setting livestream brought together creators from across Southeast Asia, who took turns using and showcasing the V80 Lite throughout the challenge. Representing four markets were Tang Makkaporn, a content creator and doctor from Thailand; Aedy Ashraf, an actor from Malaysia; Vince Domingo, founder and host of Philippine technology channel Unbox Diaries; and Tuấn Ngọc, a technology creator from Vietnam. Beyond the livestream itself, the creators used the smartphone during activities around Chiang Mai, including navigation, photography, gaming, and calls. Their participation gave the endurance challenge a regional dimension, bringing together creators with different audiences and areas of expertise around one extended test. More than 32 hours on the clock The challenge continued through day and night as the V80 Lite maintained the livestream for 32 hours and 37 minutes before completing the record attempt. The achievement comes ahead of the smartphone's official launch in the Philippines, where the V80 Lite will introduce vivo’s 10,000mAh BlueVolt Battery, the largest battery capacity ever offered by vivo globally. “Setting a world record is ultimately about the test itself — how long the device can keep going and whether it can complete the challenge without interruption,” said Liu Lu, Brand Marketing Director of vivo Philippines. “We wanted to put the V80 Lite through a demanding, measurable endurance challenge, and 32 hours and 37 minutes gave us a clear result that people can see for themselves," she added. The vivo V80 Lite will officially launch in the Philippines on October 4 at the Market! Market! by Ayala Malls. bd.title: Coway Run 2026 Celebrates a Decade of Progress as Thousands of Malaysians Run Forward Without Limits at Stadium Merdeka
bd.description: Marking a decade of momentum, the 10th edition of Coway Run continues to inspire Malaysians to pursue continuous growth and move forward without limits KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coway, the Best Life Solution Company, brought together more than 11,000 participants at Stadium Merdeka for the 10th edition of Coway Run 2026, a milestone event that celebrated a decade of inspiring Malaysians to embrace healthier lifestyles, push beyond their perceived limits and unlock their full potential. Coway Malaysia's management team officially flagging off the 10KM Run Category at Coway Run 2026, marking the start of a race dedicated to moving Forward Without Limits. Fuelled by the excitement of Coway Malaysia's 20th anniversary, this year's event carried the theme Forward Without Limits, reflecting Coway's belief that growth is an ongoing journey and that every individual has the ability to achieve more through determination, perseverance and continuous self-improvement. More than a running event, Coway Run 2026 served as a platform for people from all walks of life to challenge themselves, celebrate personal milestones and take meaningful steps towards becoming the best versions of themselves. Janice Tan, Group Manager of Marketing Division of Coway Malaysia said, "This year's Coway Run holds special significance as we celebrate both 20 years of Coway in Malaysia and 10 years of Coway Run. Over the past decade, we have seen individuals from all backgrounds come together, set new goals and push beyond what they thought was possible. At Coway, we believe that everyone possesses untapped potential, and Coway Run was created to inspire people to take that first step towards unlocking it." "The theme 'Forward Without Limits' reflects our conviction that progress is not defined by perfect conditions, but by the courage and determination to keep moving forward despite the obstacles along the way. Even in the rain, we saw many runners choosing to persevere and complete their journey, embodying the very spirit of resilience that this year's event set out to celebrate. It was inspiring to see thousands of Malaysians come together, not only to challenge themselves but also support a cause that creates a meaningful impact for communities in need," she added. With the health and safety of participants as the highest priority, Coway Run 2026 took an unexpected turn this year as the event adapted to the challenges posed by the weather and ongoing haze situation. Despite the change in format, participants from all four categories, including the 10KM Run, and modified 30KM Run, 5KM Run and 5KM Kids Run, came together with community spirit, embodying the "Forward Without Limits" philosophy. Throughout the day, the atmosphere extended beyond the race routes as participants, families and supporters immersed themselves in a vibrant race village featuring interactive activities, engaging experiences and family-friendly entertainment. The event embodied Coway's commitment to making healthy living both accessible and enjoyable, while creating opportunities for meaningful connections among communities. Inside Stadium Merdeka, visitors enjoyed a special performance by Coway's Biddy Bear mascot and dancers, followed by a live performance and exclusive meet-and-greet with popular Malaysian singer and actor Hael Husaini. Participants could also complete eight game stations to enter a grand prize lucky draw, with 10 winners taking home either a BEREX Massage Bed or BEREX Pebble Chair, while limited-edition Coway Biddy Bear hand towels were available to be won through on-ground games. In keeping with Coway's mission of helping people live healthier and happier lives, Coway Run 2026 continued to create impact beyond race day. RM10 from every ticket sold will be channeled towards the Coway Happy Water Project, an initiative dedicated to providing underserved communities with access to clean water. Through the collective efforts of participants, every registration contributed towards improving quality of life for communities in need and supporting a future where access to essential resources is within reach for all. Beyond making a meaningful difference for communities, Coway Run 2026 celebrated the perseverance and resilience demonstrated by participants in the face of unexpected circumstances. Reflecting the event's "Forward Without Limits" philosophy, runners continued to push forward and delivered inspiring performances across the competitive categories. In the Men's Open Malaysian category of the modified 30KM Run, conducted over a 10KM route, Anas Bin Rosli recorded the fastest finishing time of 00:36:27, while Michelle Ng claimed the Women's Open Malaysian title with a time of 00:54:24. In the 10KM category, Khairul Hazwan secured first place in the Men's Open Malaysian division with a time of 00:40:46, while Ee Pui Yin topped the Women's Open Malaysian category with a finishing time of 00:43:27. As Coway Run enters its second decade, the event continues to reflect Coway's commitment to empowering individuals to lead healthier lives, pursue meaningful growth and realise their potential. For more information and updates on Coway, please visit https://www.coway.com.my/ . About Coway Malaysia Coway, the Best Life Solution Company Established in 1989, Coway has been the indisputable market leader in the manufacturing and distribution of well-being household appliances in South Korea, thanks to its largest indoor water purifier manufacturing plant in the world, and state-of-the-art R&D centre in Seoul National University. Famous for its home products, Coway has been aggressively expanding its business worldwide and has over 11 million customers across the world. Besides earning recognition for its high-quality range of products, Coway is also known for its excellent after-sales customer service, and innovative easy payment plan. In 2006, Coway was introduced into the Malaysian market. Having been in Malaysia for 20 years, Coway has reached millions of Malaysian customers and has been successfully recognised as the Best Life Solution Company that strives to provide cleaner water, fresher air and better sleep; encouraging people to "Change Your Life" towards leading healthier and happier lives.

bd.title: Sino Group and SVhk Connect Start-ups with Northern Metropolis Communities Through 'Impactathon'
bd.description: To Co-create Technology Solutions for Community Well-being HONG KONG , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Northern Metropolis is steadily emerging as one of Hong Kong's key growth areas. As development gathers pace, communities have diverse and evolving needs in areas such as older adults' well-being, youth development, community connection, and social inclusion. To gain a deeper understanding of these needs and explore practical responses, Sino Inno Lab and The Spark under Sino Group have partnered with Social Ventures Hong Kong (SVhk) to launch the 'SVhk-Sino Impactathon'. The initiative brings together start-ups, universities, community organisations and residents to explore how innovation and technology can support everyday life, generating practical insights through community engagement and pilot projects to inform the Northern Metropolis's long-term development. The initiative is supported by the Northern Metropolis Co-ordination Office (NMCO) of the Development Bureau of the HKSAR Government, over 10 start-ups, six local universities, and various community partners, bringing together more than 50 partners in total. It has connected over 1,000 Northern Metropolis residents and stakeholders, including children, youth, underprivileged families, older adults and rehabilitation service users. Direct engagement has provided participating teams with valuable perspectives that have helped refine their solutions for practical application. Turning Ideas into Community Solutions Unlike conventional start-up competitions, the 'SVhk-Sino Impactathon' was designed to help innovators better understand the communities they hope to serve. Over five months, participating teams worked alongside seven community partners and engaged directly with residents to gain first-hand insights into local aspirations and community needs. The programme was supported by organisations including the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation and the Jockey Club Design Institute for Social Innovation at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, together with entrepreneurship and innovation platforms from City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Baptist University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and The University of Hong Kong. These collaborations have enabled start-ups to explore how their technologies could address community needs in real-world settings. Participating teams applied technologies including artificial intelligence ('AI'), geographic information systems ('GIS'), biotechnology and food technology to address challenges ranging from older adults' health and fall-risk prevention to youth learning and family well-being. Feedback from residents and frontline organisations has helped teams refine their solutions and improve their practical relevance. The programme also attracted start-ups from seven Asian cities, with three regional teams advancing to the finals and travelling to Hong Kong to exchange ideas with local communities and partners, while also gaining insights into the Northern Metropolis. Supporting the Development of Promising Solutions The award ceremony was held at One North in Yuen Long, where 11 teams presented their pilot projects and shared plans for future development. To support the further refinement and real-world application of selected solutions, a total of HK$200,000 in seed funding was awarded to winning teams. GOFA received the Grand Prize and Most Innovative Award for its AI-powered health risk assessment technology, while Mapcraft received the Most Community-Driven Award, and Singapore-based start-up N&E Innovations received the Most Scalable Builder Award. At the award ceremony, residents from different backgrounds, including ethnic minority communities, older adults, children, young people and families from the Northern Metropolis, were invited to experience the projects developed by participating start-ups and universities. Interactive workshops, demonstrations and sharing sessions allowed residents to explore innovative solutions first-hand and provide direct feedback to the innovators, helping inform their future development and application. Mr Ronald Cheng, Principal Assistant Secretary (Northern Metropolis) of the NMCO, who was invited to attend the award ceremony, stated, 'Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proposes that we will guide the future spatial layout of our city with the vision of the "South North Dual Engine (Finance IT)". The Northern Metropolis will be developed with the objectives of university town, I&T, industry, and environment suitable for living, work, and travel. This will require innovative thinking and cross-sector collaboration. The "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" has enabled start-up teams to step into the community, thereby understanding residents' actual needs and proposing targeted solutions. We are pleased to see that the business sector, academia, community organisations and start-ups have been working hand-in-hand on new ideas to contribute to the development of the Northern Metropolis.' Mr Francis Ngai, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of SVhk, shared, 'Community making requires both hardware and software infrastructure. While the physical infrastructure of the Northern Metropolis is gradually taking shape, its community infrastructure should be built with equal urgency to support thriving neighbourhoods. The needs of older adults, children and youth, agricultural transformation, circular economy and social inclusion also point to new reimaginations for the communities of tomorrow, and call for parallel learning and experimentation as Hong Kong advances its innovation-and-technology and talent-development priorities. The "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" brings together cross-sector partners to identify local needs, work with universities and innovation partners to find suitable solutions, and match them with frontline organisations for real-world testing and refinement. We hope each trial will generate shared learnings within the Northern Metropolis, and build, from the bottom up, the community's capacity to listen, collaborate and address challenges together.' Mr David Ng, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of Sino Group, said, 'As the Northern Metropolis continues to grow and evolve, so too do the needs of its communities. We believe the value of innovation lies not in technology alone, but in how it can improve people's lives. Building on last year's "One North STEAM AI Summer", we launched the "SVhk-Sino Impactathon" to bring together partners across government, industry, academia, research institutions and the community to explore practical solutions that support community well-being. We are grateful to all our partners, community organisations, universities, start-ups and residents for their support, and look forward to seeing these ideas continue to evolve and make a positive impact on communities across the Northern Metropolis.' The programme was supported by the Northern Metropolis Co-ordination Office of the Development Bureau of the HKSAR Government, over 10 start-ups, six local universities and various community partners, bringing together more than 50 partners in total. Through interactive workshops, technology experience booths, and demonstrations, the ‘SVhk-Sino Impactathon’ enabled participants to explore innovative technologies in an engaging, interactive setting.

Dragonpass: AI Is Shifting the Membership Economy from Perks Redemption to Personalized Experiences
bd.description: HANGZHOU, China , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As interest-based travel reshapes global mobility—with consumers increasingly traveling for concerts, exhibitions and sporting events while seeking immersive experiences and emotional value—the membership economy is evolving from "perks redemption" toward deeper user value management. Speaking at the 2026 Apsara Conference's "AI Going Global Growth Summit" in Hangzhou, Jane Zhu, Co-founder and CEO of Dragonpass Group, shared insights into how AI is redefining travel and lifestyle services. Jane Zhu shared insights into how AI is redefining travel and lifestyle services As a global company connecting more than 800 corporate clients with over 40 million members, Dragonpass is experiencing this shift firsthand. Zhu noted that AI enables the company to better understand user preferences and integrate membership benefits into real travel scenarios. Through conversational AI, travelers can share their interests and receive itinerary recommendations matched with relevant airport benefits, transfers and local services—shifting the service model from searching for available benefits to generating services around what users want to do. "AI expands the boundaries of what our services can deliver, while human expertise preserves the warmth of service. Through human-AI collaboration, we can redefine high-quality service experiences," Zhu stated. As part of this evolution, Dragonpass has partnered with Alibaba Cloud to launch its AI Airport Concierge, leveraging the capabilities of Qwen large language models and Dragonpass's long-established global airport service network. The service brings AI capabilities into one of the most frequent touchpoints in the travel journey, integrating airport resources and services into an intelligent experience. Eight months after launch, the AI Airport Concierge has served more than 100,000 travelers. Dragonpass is also extending its AI-powered service capabilities beyond the airport, with broader intelligent travel and lifestyle services set to roll out across markets including Brazil, South Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific. Looking ahead, Dragonpass remains committed to driving user engagement through AI, with the aim of delivering more intelligent, personalized and end-to-end travel and lifestyle experiences globally. About Dragonpass Established in 2005, Dragonpass is a leading global travel and lifestyle platform, providing premium benefits and experiences to more than 40 million members worldwide. Its growing ecosystem spans travel, health and wellness, lifestyle and entertainment, with a global network covering more than 140 countries and regions and partnerships with more than 800 enterprises. ae.title: Coway Run 2026 Celebrates a Decade of Progress as Thousands of Malaysians Run Forward Without Limits at Stadium Merdeka
ae.description: Marking a decade of momentum, the 10th edition of Coway Run continues to inspire Malaysians to pursue continuous growth and move forward without limits KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia , Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Coway, the Best Life Solution Company, brought together more than 11,000 participants at Stadium Merdeka for the 10th edition of Coway Run 2026, a milestone event that celebrated a decade of inspiring Malaysians to embrace healthier lifestyles, push beyond their perceived limits and unlock their full potential. Coway Malaysia's management team officially flagging off the 10KM Run Category at Coway Run 2026, marking the start of a race dedicated to moving Forward Without Limits. Fuelled by the excitement of Coway Malaysia's 20th anniversary, this year's event carried the theme Forward Without Limits, reflecting Coway's belief that growth is an ongoing journey and that every individual has the ability to achieve more through determination, perseverance and continuous self-improvement. More than a running event, Coway Run 2026 served as a platform for people from all walks of life to challenge themselves, celebrate personal milestones and take meaningful steps towards becoming the best versions of themselves. Janice Tan, Group Manager of Marketing Division of Coway Malaysia said, "This year's Coway Run holds special significance as we celebrate both 20 years of Coway in Malaysia and 10 years of Coway Run. Over the past decade, we have seen individuals from all backgrounds come together, set new goals and push beyond what they thought was possible. At Coway, we believe that everyone possesses untapped potential, and Coway Run was created to inspire people to take that first step towards unlocking it." "The theme 'Forward Without Limits' reflects our conviction that progress is not defined by perfect conditions, but by the courage and determination to keep moving forward despite the obstacles along the way. Even in the rain, we saw many runners choosing to persevere and complete their journey, embodying the very spirit of resilience that this year's event set out to celebrate. It was inspiring to see thousands of Malaysians come together, not only to challenge themselves but also support a cause that creates a meaningful impact for communities in need," she added. With the health and safety of participants as the highest priority, Coway Run 2026 took an unexpected turn this year as the event adapted to the challenges posed by the weather and ongoing haze situation. Despite the change in format, participants from all four categories, including the 10KM Run, and modified 30KM Run, 5KM Run and 5KM Kids Run, came together with community spirit, embodying the "Forward Without Limits" philosophy. Throughout the day, the atmosphere extended beyond the race routes as participants, families and supporters immersed themselves in a vibrant race village featuring interactive activities, engaging experiences and family-friendly entertainment. The event embodied Coway's commitment to making healthy living both accessible and enjoyable, while creating opportunities for meaningful connections among communities. Inside Stadium Merdeka, visitors enjoyed a special performance by Coway's Biddy Bear mascot and dancers, followed by a live performance and exclusive meet-and-greet with popular Malaysian singer and actor Hael Husaini. Participants could also complete eight game stations to enter a grand prize lucky draw, with 10 winners taking home either a BEREX Massage Bed or BEREX Pebble Chair, while limited-edition Coway Biddy Bear hand towels were available to be won through on-ground games. In keeping with Coway's mission of helping people live healthier and happier lives, Coway Run 2026 continued to create impact beyond race day. RM10 from every ticket sold will be channeled towards the Coway Happy Water Project, an initiative dedicated to providing underserved communities with access to clean water. Through the collective efforts of participants, every registration contributed towards improving quality of life for communities in need and supporting a future where access to essential resources is within reach for all. Beyond making a meaningful difference for communities, Coway Run 2026 celebrated the perseverance and resilience demonstrated by participants in the face of unexpected circumstances. Reflecting the event's "Forward Without Limits" philosophy, runners continued to push forward and delivered inspiring performances across the competitive categories. In the Men's Open Malaysian category of the modified 30KM Run, conducted over a 10KM route, Anas Bin Rosli recorded the fastest finishing time of 00:36:27, while Michelle Ng claimed the Women's Open Malaysian title with a time of 00:54:24. In the 10KM category, Khairul Hazwan secured first place in the Men's Open Malaysian division with a time of 00:40:46, while Ee Pui Yin topped the Women's Open Malaysian category with a finishing time of 00:43:27. As Coway Run enters its second decade, the event continues to reflect Coway's commitment to empowering individuals to lead healthier lives, pursue meaningful growth and realise their potential. For more information and updates on Coway, please visit https://www.coway.com.my/ . About Coway Malaysia Coway, the Best Life Solution Company Established in 1989, Coway has been the indisputable market leader in the manufacturing and distribution of well-being household appliances in South Korea, thanks to its largest indoor water purifier manufacturing plant in the world, and state-of-the-art R&D centre in Seoul National University. Famous for its home products, Coway has been aggressively expanding its business worldwide and has over 11 million customers across the world. Besides earning recognition for its high-quality range of products, Coway is also known for its excellent after-sales customer service, and innovative easy payment plan. In 2006, Coway was introduced into the Malaysian market. Having been in Malaysia for 20 years, Coway has reached millions of Malaysian customers and has been successfully recognised as the Best Life Solution Company that strives to provide cleaner water, fresher air and better sleep; encouraging people to "Change Your Life" towards leading healthier and happier lives.
